title: He Has Won Four Champions Leagues. On Saturday Night, Ancelotti's Brazil Faces the Team That Stunned the World in 2022.
excerpt: Brazil vs Morocco at MetLife Stadium is the biggest match of the World Cup's opening weekend. For NRIs in the New York-New Jersey corridor, it is happening in their backyard.
body:
Carlo Ancelotti has managed Real Madrid through countless European nights. He has won the Champions League four times. He has coached Zinedine Zidane, Cristiano Ronaldo, David Beckham, and Andrea Pirlo. None of that guarantees what happens on Saturday night at MetLife Stadium.

Brazil vs Morocco kicks off at 6 PM Eastern in East Rutherford, New Jersey — the biggest match of the World Cup's opening weekend, and arguably the most consequential group-stage game of the entire first round.

## Two Teams, Two Missions

Brazil arrives as a five-time world champion desperate to prove it still belongs in that conversation. The Selecao have not won the World Cup since 2002 — a 24-year drought that weighs heavily on a football-obsessed nation. The quarter-final exit in Qatar, where Croatia eliminated them on penalties, remains a wound that has not fully healed.

Under Ancelotti, who took charge in early 2024, Brazil has found something resembling structure. The Italian's 4-2-4 system is designed to unleash Vinicius Junior, Raphinha, Matheus Cunha, and Endrick simultaneously — an attacking quartet that, on paper, should terrify any defence in the world. In warm-up matches against Panama and Egypt, Brazil looked cohesive and dangerous.

Morocco, on the other hand, arrives with nothing to lose and everything to prove. The Atlas Lions' 2022 World Cup semifinal run — when they became the first African team to reach the last four — was one of the great stories in tournament history. They beat Belgium, Spain, and Portugal along the way, and they did it with organisation, fearlessness, and the ferocious support of the Moroccan diaspora.

This time, Morocco are reigning Africa Cup of Nations champions, controversially declared title-holders earlier this year. They have the pedigree and the belief.

## The Ancelotti Factor

What makes Brazil genuinely different this cycle is the man on the touchline. Previous managers struggled to balance the egos and the expectations of coaching the Selecao. Ancelotti, with his laissez-faire management style and decades of experience with elite performers, has managed to create calm where chaos usually reigns.

"There have been far superior Brazilian rosters," Sports Illustrated noted, "but not for decades has the Selecao been led so expertly on the touchline." Ancelotti's ability to man-manage superstars is perhaps his greatest asset. Vinicius Jr, who can be volatile and brilliant in equal measure, has looked more focused and disciplined under the Italian's guidance.

## Morocco's Injury Cloud

Morocco is not at full strength. The squad suffered injuries during their draw with Norway in a warm-up match, and the recent managerial change has introduced some uncertainty. But dismissing this team at your peril is a lesson Belgium, Spain, and Portugal learned the hard way four years ago.

Achraf Hakimi remains one of the best right-backs on the planet. The defence, while less experienced than 2022, retains its organisational discipline. And the Atlas Lions' counter-attacking speed — the weapon that undid Portugal at the last World Cup — is still razor-sharp.

## A Night for the NRI Community

For the Indian diaspora in the New York and New Jersey corridor — one of the densest NRI populations in the United States — Saturday night is a spectacle. MetLife Stadium sits in East Rutherford, less than ten miles from the heart of Jersey City's Little India on Newark Avenue, where Edison's Oak Tree Road meets the world's game.

This is not India's match, but it is India's neighbourhood. Thousands of NRIs with World Cup tickets will experience the atmosphere firsthand. Brazil's massive global following and Morocco's passionate diaspora support guarantee a full, loud, electric stadium.

For those without tickets, watch parties are running across northern New Jersey and New York City. FOX has the broadcast, with streaming available on Peacock and Fubo.

## The Verdict

Bookmakers have Brazil as favourites at -145, with Morocco at +450 and a draw at +275. Most preview sites predict a Brazil win, with scorelines ranging from 2-1 to 3-1. The consensus: Brazil's attacking talent will eventually overwhelm Morocco, but the Atlas Lions will not go quietly.

The last competitive meeting between these teams was at France '98, when Ronaldo, Rivaldo, and Bebeto powered a 3-0 Brazil win. Twenty-eight years later, the gap has closed dramatically. Morocco is not the same team, and neither is Brazil.

Kickoff is at 3 PM Pacific, 6 PM Eastern. The World Cup is in your backyard. Watch this one.

*Sources: FIFA.com, FOX Sports, Sports Illustrated, CBS Sports*
